summary.text: 告 commonly means “tell,” “report,” “announce,” “inform,” or “accuse.” Its early graphic construction is disputed: one proposal derives it from 舌 by extending the central stroke upward to depict a tongue projecting from a mouth and connect it with speaking or telling; other accounts analyze 牛 plus 口, or 口 plus an abbreviated 壴.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. One proposal treats the whole graph as a pictorial form derived from 舌: its central stroke is extended upward to depict a tongue projecting from a mouth, associated with speaking or telling. The received Shuowen account analyzes 牛 plus 口 and explains an ox striking a person while a crossbar restrains its horns as a way of signaling people. A separate proposal analyzes 口 plus an abbreviated 壴; 壴 may be phonetic and possibly semantic, but its function is uncertain.

history.text: The received Shuowen explanation analyzes 告 as 牛 plus 口 and interprets it as an ox striking a person while a crossbar restrains its horns, thereby informing people. This historical lexicographic account does not confirm the construction of earlier forms.

A later graphic account describes the seal form as abbreviated during clerical transformation and regularized into the modern form. The curated image is a modern redraw of the seal form transmitted in the Shuowen tradition; it illustrates that later form but does not settle competing explanations of earlier forms.

uncertainties.text: The early construction remains unresolved among a whole-graph tongue picture derived from 舌, the Shuowen 牛-plus-口 explanation, and the reported 口-plus-abbreviated-壴 proposal. The 壴 proposal is available here from an article abstract, and its function is uncertain.

A Southwestern Mandarin word meaning “try” or “check out” is reported as written 告 through borrowing from 校. Similar Middle Chinese readings are reported, but the proposed direction and sound pathway are unverified; the 1909 example attests the regional use, not its derivation.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone and later examples reported; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: A reported oracle-bone example concerns a deer report, and later examples use 告 for reporting or telling. These attestations do not establish one original meaning or a sequence of semantic change.

senses.period: Western Zhou examples reported; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: Western Zhou bronze examples are reported with uses for reporting and admonishing. Their development from earlier senses is not established.

senses.period: Western Zhou examples reported; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: Accusatory use is reported among Western Zhou bronze examples; its relationship to “report” is not established.
Current uses include telling, announcing, informing, and accusing. The supplied glosses do not establish their chronology or semantic connections.

A Southwestern Mandarin use meaning “try” or “check out” is attested in a 1909 example. One proposed account is that 告 borrowed the graph for 校 to write a similar-sounding word, rather than developing this meaning from “tell.” The borrowing direction and sound pathway remain uncertain.

limitations.text: The cited examples do not establish a sequence connecting sacrificial, reporting, admonishing, accusatory, and telling uses.
The proposed borrowing from 校 lacks independent confirmation of its source account and historical sound pathway; similarity alone does not establish the borrowing direction.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Lexical Database)
evidence.field: 甲骨文構形分析；商代及後續用例
evidence.text: This database presents Zhang Yujin’s account that oracle-bone 告 is derived from 舌 by extending its central stroke upward, representing an open mouth with tongue and giving the sense ‘speak/tell’; it also records a 牛+口 sacrificial interpretation as an alternative. It cites oracle-bone 合集1166甲 for 告 used as a sacrificial term read 祰, 屯南997 for a report of a deer, Western Zhou bronze examples for reporting, admonishing, and accusing, and a Guodian Chu slip example for ‘tell’. These are source-reported examples, not a proven chronological sequence of semantic change.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: 陳美蘭, ‘說「告」’ (2013), abstract hosted by 元照/月旦知識庫
evidence.field: 古文字構形分析與異說
evidence.text: The abstract surveys competing explanations: the traditional Shuowen 牛+口 account; Zhang Yujin’s proposal that 告 derives from 舌; and the author’s proposal that oracle-bone 告 is 口 plus an abbreviated 壴, possibly a phonetic element and possibly also semantic. The author says this proposal better fits parallel variation between the upper part of 告 and 壴-type graphs, while acknowledging uncertainty about that component’s function. The full paper PDF appeared in search but opening it was rejected; this item reports only the inspected abstract.
evidence.title: 說「告」- 元照出版, 月旦知識庫

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 text quoted in Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 告異體研訂瀏覽；Shuowen gloss and later form account
evidence.text: The cited Shuowen account says 告 depicts an ox striking a person, with its horns held by a crossbar, thereby informing people, and analyzes the graph as 牛 plus 口. The Ministry entry describes the seal form as transforming through clerical abbreviation and regular-script shaping into the modern graph. This is a historical lexicographic explanation and later graphic account, not independent confirmation of the Shang graph’s parts.

evidence.source: Wiktionary, English 告 entry
evidence.field: Glyph origin; historical phonology; modern readings
evidence.text: The entry labels the graph’s origin unclear and reports competing interpretations: Xu Zhongshu’s protruding tongue pictogram, Chen Meilan’s abbreviated 壴 plus 口 analysis, and the Shuowen 牛+口 account, with Yu Xingwu’s objection that the upper part is not 牛 in oracle-bone and bronze forms. It gives Standard Mandarin gào, Cantonese Jyutping gou3, Baxter Middle Chinese kawH (Guangyun 古到切), Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *kˤuk-s, and Zhengzhang Old Chinese *kuːɡs. It separately lists a checked Middle Chinese reading kowk and Baxter–Sagart *kˤuk. These reconstructions concern the character/word readings and do not settle the graphic analysis.

evidence.field: 甲骨文構形分析；商代及後續用例
evidence.text: This database presents Zhang Yujin’s account that oracle-bone 告 is derived from 舌 by extending its central stroke upward, representing an open mouth with tongue and giving the sense ‘speak/tell’; it also records a 牛+口 sacrificial interpretation as an alternative. It cites oracle-bone 合集1166甲 for 告 used as a sacrificial term read 祰, 屯南997 for a report of a deer, Western Zhou bronze examples for reporting, admonishing, and accusing, and a Guodian Chu slip example for ‘tell’. evidence.source: 陳美蘭, ‘說「告」’ (2013), abstract hosted by 元照/月旦知識庫
evidence.field: 古文字構形分析與異說
evidence.text: The abstract surveys competing explanations: the traditional Shuowen 牛+口 account; Zhang Yujin’s proposal that 告 derives from 舌; and the author’s proposal that oracle-bone 告 is 口 plus an abbreviated 壴, possibly a phonetic element and possibly also semantic. The author says this proposal better fits parallel variation between the upper part of 告 and 壴-type graphs, while acknowledging uncertainty about that component’s function. The full paper PDF appeared in search but opening it was rejected; this item reports only the inspected abstract.

gaps: The oracle-bone and bronze glyph images were not visually inspected. Though the sources cite Shang-period examples, I cannot independently date or compare the actual graph shapes here.

Graphic origin remains disputed: the Shuowen 牛+口 account is a Han lexicographic interpretation; tongue-derived and 壴+口 proposals are later analyses. The consulted sources do not establish a consensus or a secure account of the top element’s earliest referent.

The database’s claimed early sacrificial use read 祰 is not itself evidence that the graph was originally a sacrificial pictogram; its relation to the later ‘report/tell’ sense is not established as a chronological sequence. The sources supply examples from Shang, Western Zhou, and Warring States materials but not a complete dated semantic history.
No independently verified dated first attestation for 告 was established; Shang oracle-bone context is reported by the database, but artifact-level dates for cited examples were not checked.

The whole-graph regional borrowing claim from 校 remains under-sourced here: the cited Yang (2010) source was not located, and an independently inspected 校 historical-pronunciation record was not obtained. The shared Middle Chinese form alone does not establish borrowing direction or the specific phonological development.

The dossier’s Thai cognate claim for 告 is not independently assessed: this search did not locate a primary comparative Tai-Chinese source or independently establish Thai กล่าว’s historical form, chronology, or a regular sound correspondence.

The dossier lists GSR series 1039 and Zhengzhang readings; this research did not independently consult primary GSR/Guangyun editions or validate those series assignments. No sound component is securely identified in the proposed graphic analyses, so a component-by-component phonetic comparison cannot be supplied.
The cited 2013 article’s full text was inaccessible through the attempted PDF URL. Findings on its 壴+口 proposal come from the inspected abstract only.

No character-specific glyph image was selected: Commons surfaced 告-oracle.svg but the category and file page could not be opened, so its exact image URL, identity, provenance, and licensing remain unverified. A generic CC0 oracle-bone tracing was inspected but not identified as 告.
The official Sinica query interface and official CC0 notice were inspected, but this invocation did not obtain a specific 告 query result/image URL. No Sinica glyph image is proposed.

The graph’s origin remains disputed. Shuowen’s ox-and-mouth account is a historical Han lexicographic explanation; tongue-derived and 壴-plus-mouth analyses are later scholarly proposals. Available pages do not establish a consensus, and the identity of the early upper element is unresolved.
